title: A proper morphism is a limit of proper morphisms over schemes of finite type over Z
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then there are a directed set $\Lambda$ and an inverse system $(f_\lambda:X_\lambda\to S_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ of morphisms of schemes (transition morphisms $X_\lambda\to X_\mu$, $S_\lambda\to S_\mu$ for $\lambda\ge\mu$, commuting with $f_\lambda,f_\mu$) such that: the transition morphisms $X_\lambda\to X_\mu$ and $S_\lambda\to S_\mu$ are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; every $f_\lambda$ is proper; every $S_\lambda$ is of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; and $(X\to S)=\varprojlim_\lambda(X_\lambda\to S_\lambda)$, i.e. $X=\varprojlim_\lambda X_\lambda$ and $S=\varprojlim_\lambda S_\lambda$ in the category of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], with $f$ the limit of the $f_\lambda$. If moreover $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, the system can be chosen with every $S_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}A_\lambda$ affine, $A_\lambda$ a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra (generated as a ring by finitely many elements); then $A=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0P (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, line 3346) and its proof (Lemma 09ZR proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, absolute Noetherian approximation Proposition 01ZA, Lemmas 01ZM descend-finite-presentation and 081F eventually-proper (tag 0A0P checked in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags line 12642); 'some details omitted'); the affine clause: in the proof the $S_j$ come from absolute Noetherian approximation, which for affine $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the system of finitely generated subrings of $A$ (proof of 01ZA), and it is the form in which Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (pione.tex, 'General case', line ~1851), cites 0A0P ('with $S_i$ affine and of finite type over $\mathbf Z$')

proof.text: *A proper finitely presented envelope.* Since $f$ is proper and $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-in-proper-fp] $X=\varprojlim_{k\in K}X_k$ with every $X_k\to S$ proper and of finite presentation and every $X\to X_k$ a closed immersion. Fix one $k_0\in K$ ($K$ is nonempty) and put $Y=X_{k_0}$, $g:Y\to S$ its structure morphism and $\iota:X\to Y$ the closed immersion; thus $g\circ\iota=f$, $g$ is proper and of finite presentation. (Stacks uses the whole system $(X_k)_k$; the construction below needs only this one envelope, see step 5.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0P (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, line 3346), proof, first sentence (Lemma 09ZR)

proof.text: *Absolute Noetherian approximation of $S$.* By [prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system] (Stacks Proposition 01ZA; Lean closed) $S$ admits a Noetherian approximation [def-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system]: a small cofiltered category, a diagram of schemes of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with affine transition morphisms, and a limit cone with vertex $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] it is re-indexed by a nonempty directed set $J$: an inverse system $(S_j,s_{jj'})_{j\in J}$ of schemes of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with affine transition morphisms $s_{j'j}:S_{j'}\to S_j$ ($j'\ge j$) [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and projections $q_j:S\to S_j$ exhibiting $S=\varprojlim_jS_j$. Each $S_j$ is quasi-compact (finite type) and Noetherian (finite type over the Noetherian ring $\mathbf Z$), hence quasi-separated; each $q_j$ and each $s_{j'j}$ is affine [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. If $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, use instead [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine] (Lean closed): $J$ is the set of finitely generated subrings $A_j\subseteq A$ ordered by inclusion (a directed set: $A_j,A_{j'}\subseteq A_j[A_{j'}]$), $S_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$, transitions induced by the inclusions, and $\operatorname{Spec}A=\varprojlim_j\operatorname{Spec}A_j$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0P (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, line 3346), proof, second sentence (Proposition 01ZA, proof of 01ZA for the affine case)

proof.text: *Descending the envelope.* $g:Y\to S$ is of finite presentation and the $S_j$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated with affine transitions, so by [thm-pd-spreading-out] (1) (Stacks Lemma 01ZM; the source repository's sorry-free AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation) there are $j_0\in J$, a morphism of finite presentation $g_{j_0}:Y_{j_0}\to S_{j_0}$ and an isomorphism $Y\cong Y_{j_0}\times_{S_{j_0}}S$ over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; transport $\iota$ along it. For $j\ge j_0$ put $Y_j=Y_{j_0}\times_{S_{j_0}}S_j$ with $g_j:Y_j\to S_j$ the projection; then $Y=Y_j\times_{S_j}S$ (transitivity of fibre products), with projection $t_j:Y\to Y_j$, and for $j'\ge j\ge j_0$ the transition $y_{j'j}:Y_{j'}=Y_j\times_{S_j}S_{j'}\to Y_j$ is the base change of $s_{j'j}$, hence affine; likewise $t_j$ is the base change of the affine $q_j$, hence affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. $Y_{j_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: $g_{j_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (finite presentation) and $S_{j_0}$ is.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0P (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, line 3346), proof, third sentence (Lemma 01ZM)

proof.text: *Making the model proper.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper] (Stacks Lemma 081F) to the system $(S_j)_{j\ge j_0}$ (directed, affine transitions, limit $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory], the subset $\{j\ge j_0\}$ being cofinal), with $0=j_0$, $X_0=Y_{j_0}$, $Y_0=S_{j_0}$ and $f_0=g_{j_0}$: $S_{j_0}$, $Y_{j_0}$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated (steps 2, 3), $g_{j_0}$ is locally of finite type (it is of finite presentation), and its base change to $S$ is $g$, which is proper. So $g_{j_1}$ is proper for some $j_1\ge j_0$; replace $j_0$ by $j_1$. Then for every $j\ge j_0$ the morphism $g_j$, a base change of $g_{j_0}$, is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0P (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, line 3346), proof, fourth sentence (Lemma 081F)

proof.text: *The stages: scheme-theoretic images of $X$.* (This step and the next two fill in the construction of the system that Stacks leaves out ('Some details omitted'); Stacks indexes the system by pairs $(k,j)$ with $X_{k,j}$ a descended model of $X_k$; here, written by the agent, the stages are the scheme-theoretic images of $X$ in the proper models $Y_j$ of the single envelope $Y$, which needs no choices of compatible descents.) Let $\Lambda=\{j\in J: j\ge j_0\}$, a directed set, cofinal in $J$. For $j\in\Lambda$ let $h_j=t_j\circ\iota:X\to Y_j$; it is affine (a closed immersion followed by the affine $t_j$), hence quasi-compact. Let $Z_j\subseteq Y_j$ be its scheme-theoretic image [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel], with closed immersion $\iota_j:Z_j\to Y_j$ and $p_j:X\to Z_j$, $\iota_j\circ p_j=h_j$; for every affine open $U\subseteq Y_j$ the ideal of $Z_j$ on $U$ is $K_j(U)=\ker(\mathcal O(U)\to\mathcal O(h_j^{-1}U))$. Put $f_j=g_j\circ\iota_j:Z_j\to S_j$: a closed immersion followed by the proper $g_j$ (step 4), hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0P (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, line 3346), proof, 'The set I will consist of these pairs (k,j) ... Some details omitted' (construction replaced, written by the agent)

proof.text: *Transition morphisms.* Let $j'\ge j$ in $\Lambda$ and $c=y_{j'j}\circ\iota_{j'}:Z_{j'}\to Y_j$ (affine: a closed immersion followed by an affine morphism, so quasi-compact). For an affine open $U\subseteq Y_j$, $V=y_{j'j}^{-1}U$ is affine, $h_{j'}^{-1}V=h_j^{-1}U$ (since $y_{j'j}\circ h_{j'}=h_j$), and $\mathcal O(U)\to\mathcal O(h_j^{-1}U)$ factors as $\mathcal O(U)\to\mathcal O(V)\to\mathcal O(V)/K_{j'}(V)=\mathcal O(Z_{j'}\cap V)\to\mathcal O(h_{j'}^{-1}V)$, the last map injective by the description of $K_{j'}(V)$ as a kernel; so $\ker(\mathcal O(U)\to\mathcal O(c^{-1}U))=K_j(U)$. By the universal property of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] (2) applied to the quasi-compact morphism $c$ (whose image ideal is $K_j$, not smaller) and the closed immersion $\iota_j$, there is a unique $u_{j'j}:Z_{j'}\to Z_j$ with $\iota_j\circ u_{j'j}=y_{j'j}\circ\iota_{j'}$. Since $\iota_j$ is a monomorphism, $u_{jj}=\mathrm{id}$, $u_{j'j}\circ u_{j''j'}=u_{j''j}$, $u_{j'j}\circ p_{j'}=p_j$ (both composed with $\iota_j$ give $h_j$), and $f_j\circ u_{j'j}=g_j\circ y_{j'j}\circ\iota_{j'}=s_{j'j}\circ f_{j'}$. So $(f_j:Z_j\to S_j)_{j\in\Lambda}$ is an inverse system of morphisms and $(p_j)$, $(q_j)$ are compatible cones with $f_j\circ p_j=g_j\circ t_j\circ\iota=q_j\circ g\circ\iota=q_j\circ f$. The transition $u_{j'j}$ is affine: it factors as $Z_{j'}\to Z_j\times_{S_j}S_{j'}\to Z_j$, where the first map $r=(u_{j'j},f_{j'})$ composed with the closed immersion $e=\iota_j\times_{S_j}S_{j'}:Z_j\times_{S_j}S_{j'}\to Y_j\times_{S_j}S_{j'}=Y_{j'}$ is $\iota_{j'}$, a closed immersion, and $e$ is separated (a closed immersion), so $r$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-from-composite], and the second is the base change of the affine $s_{j'j}$; closed immersions are affine and composites of affine morphisms are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. The transitions $s_{j'j}$ of $(S_j)_{j\in\Lambda}$ are affine by step 2.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0P (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, line 3346), proof, 'For every k' >= k we can find a j' >= j and a morphism ... These morphisms form the transition morphisms of the system' (agent's version)

proof.text: *$X$ is the limit of the $Z_j$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] the limit $L=\varprojlim_{j\in\Lambda}Z_j$ exists (affine transitions, step 6); the cone $(p_j)$ gives $\varphi:X\to L$. Cover $Y_{j_0}$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ each mapping into an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R_0\subseteq S_{j_0}$. For $j\in\Lambda$ the preimage $U_j$ of $U$ in $S_j$ is affine, $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}R_j$ (transitions affine), and the preimage of $U$ in $S$ is $\varprojlim_jU_j=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R=\varinjlim_jR_j$ (open-preimage and affine clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit]). The preimages of $W$ are $W_j=W\times_UU_j=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{R_0}R_j)$ in $Y_j$ and $W_S=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{R_0}R)$ in $Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $B\otimes_{R_0}R=\varinjlim_j B\otimes_{R_0}R_j$ (tensor products commute with colimits) [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. $X\cap W_S=\iota^{-1}W_S=\operatorname{Spec}((B\otimes R)/\mathfrak a)$ for an ideal $\mathfrak a$ (a closed subscheme of an affine scheme), and $h_j^{-1}W_j=X\cap W_S$, so by step 5 $Z_j\cap W_j=\operatorname{Spec}(C_j)$, $C_j=(B\otimes R_j)/K_j$ with $K_j=\ker(B\otimes R_j\to(B\otimes R)/\mathfrak a)$. The induced map $\varinjlim_jC_j\to(B\otimes R)/\mathfrak a$ is injective (a filtered colimit of injective maps $C_j\hookrightarrow(B\otimes R)/\mathfrak a$) and surjective (every element of $B\otimes R$ comes from some $B\otimes R_j$), hence an isomorphism. The preimage of the open $\iota_{j_0}^{-1}W\subseteq Z_{j_0}$ in $Z_j$ is $Z_j\cap W_j$, so by the open-preimage clause of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] its preimage in $L$ is $\varprojlim_j(Z_j\cap W_j)=\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_jC_j)$, and $\varphi$ restricted to $X\cap W_S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the isomorphism above. These opens cover $X$ and $L$ ($W$ runs over a cover of $Y_{j_0}$), so $\varphi$ is an isomorphism: $X=\varprojlim_{j\in\Lambda}Z_j$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0P (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, line 3346), proof, '(X -> S) = lim (X_i -> S_i)' (written out by the agent)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Index by $\Lambda$: $X_\lambda=Z_\lambda$, $S_\lambda=S_\lambda$, $f_\lambda$ as in step 5. The transition morphisms of both systems are affine (steps 2, 6), every $f_\lambda$ is proper (step 5), every $S_\lambda$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ (step 2), $X=\varprojlim_\lambda X_\lambda$ (step 7), $S=\varprojlim_{\lambda\in\Lambda}S_\lambda$ (restriction to the cofinal $\Lambda$, [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory]), and $f$ is the limit of the $f_\lambda$: it is the unique morphism $X\to S$ with $q_\lambda\circ f=f_\lambda\circ p_\lambda$ for all $\lambda$ (step 6).

proof.text: *Affine case.* If $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, step 2 used the finitely generated subrings $A_j\subseteq A$, so every $S_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}A_\lambda$ ($\lambda\in\Lambda$) is affine with $A_\lambda$ a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra. $A$ is the directed union of its finitely generated subrings (each $a\in A$ lies in $\mathbf Z[a]$), i.e. $A=\varinjlim_{j\in J}A_j$ with the inclusions as coprojections [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (in the source repository: CommRingCat.isColimitFgSubalgebraCocone, sorry-free), and restricting to the cofinal $\Lambda$ gives $A=\varinjlim_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda$ [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory]; the identification $\operatorname{Spec}A=\varprojlim_\lambda\operatorname{Spec}A_\lambda$ of step 8 is the one of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit].

split_report.summary: Tag 0A0P confirmed (tags line 12642, limits.tex line 3346). Stacks' proof: 09ZR (X closed in proper finitely presented X_k), absolute Noetherian approximation 01ZA, descent of finitely presented X_k by 01ZM, properness by 081F, transition morphisms by 01ZM, 'some details omitted'. The caution of the brief is right and Stacks handles it exactly so: X itself is not descended (not of finite presentation), only the finitely presented proper envelopes X_k. The omitted details (a compatible choice of descents indexed by pairs (k,j)) are replaced by an agent-written construction from one envelope Y=X_{k0}: descend Y to a proper Y_j0 over S_j0 and take Z_j = scheme-theoretic image of X in Y_j; the transitions are forced by the universal property, and X = lim Z_j by an affine-local colimit computation. Nine steps; new nodes: lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-in-proper-fp (09ZR, unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper (081F, unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel (Mathlib leaf, Scheme.Hom.image/ker_apply/IsClosedImmersion.lift). 01ZA and its affine case are the closed nodes prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system and lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine (cofiltered category re-indexed by the reviewed leaf lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex); 01ZM is thm-pd-spreading-out. The affine clause comes from using the finitely generated subrings in step 2.

lean.statement: theorem exists_proper_limit_noetherian {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] : ∃ (Λ : Type u) (_ : Preorder Λ) (_ : Nonempty Λ) (_ : IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)) (Xs Ss : Λᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (fs : Xs ⟶ Ss) (πX : (Functor.const Λᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ Xs) (πS : (Functor.const Λᵒᵖ).obj S ⟶ Ss), Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X πX)) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk S πS)) ∧ (∀ (i j : Λᵒᵖ) (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (Xs.map a) ∧ IsAffineHom (Ss.map a)) ∧ (∀ i : Λᵒᵖ, IsProper (fs.app i)) ∧ (∀ i : Λᵒᵖ, LocallyOfFiniteType (specULiftZIsTerminal.from (Ss.obj i)) ∧ QuasiCompact (specULiftZIsTerminal.from (Ss.obj i))) ∧ (∀ i : Λᵒᵖ, πX.app i ≫ fs.app i = f ≫ πS.app i) ∧ (IsAffine S → (∀ i : Λᵒᵖ, IsAffine (Ss.obj i) ∧ RingHom.FiniteType (algebraMap ℤ (Scheme.Γ.obj (Opposite.op (Ss.obj i))))) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Scheme.Γ.mapCocone (Cone.mk S πS).op)))
